kevin: FYI saw ~40% of asia-east1 GPU spot nodes drain in ~6m, autoscaler lagged, a bunch of pods bounced to on-demand and left nodepool-proxy taints in place. posting graphs + events. cc @ajay @sophie @infra-bot

ajay: link to grafana? which pools exactly?

kevin: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/singleshot/gpu-evictions?orgId=1
Pools: gpu-asia-spot-a and gpu-asia-spot-b. Events snippet:
```
Events:
  2026-03-17T11:02:14Z Node gpu-asia-spot-a-23 Preempted by cloudprovider
  2026-03-17T11:02:16Z Pod evict: pod/model-worker-7c8fb, gracePeriodSeconds=30
  2026-03-17T11:03:05Z ClusterAutoscaler ScaleUp: launched instance gpu-on-demand-xx (az=asia-east1-a)
  2026-03-17T11:03:50Z Node gpu-asia-spot-a-23 cordoned but taint persisted: node-role/proxy=standby:NoSchedule
```

sophie: we've seen this pattern before — the mixture of spot machine types + fast eviction waves leaves leftover taints/proxy nodes that block rescheduling for a minute. two quick mitigations: add a short "gracefulDriftWindow" to autoscaler (60-120s) to accept temporary imbalance, and a tiny warm standby of tainted on-demand proxy nodes per AZ that have tolerations for eviction-manager pods.

ajay: Example toleration/taint pattern I'm thinking of:
```yaml
# node pool template for warm-standby
nodePool:
  name: gpu-warm-standby-asia
  taints:
    - key: node-role/proxy
      value: standby
      effect: NoSchedule
  size: 2  # one per AZ minimum

# pod toleration for the proxy daemonset
tolerations:
  - key: "node-role/proxy"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "standby"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```

ajay: Also add scaleDownDelaySeconds: 600 on autoscaler for these standby pools so we don't kill them during spot churn.

kevin: cost hit if we keep 2 warm proxies in asia is ~+2-3% monthly GPU spend but buys us stable tail latency (avoids 7-12s cold reschedule hits per request). worth it for latency-sensitive routes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: triggered job infra/standby-proxy/validate-staging (run id: 20260317-09). Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jenkins/job/standby-proxy/20260317-09/console

sophie: i'll draft a short RFC and update the ops runbook with a playbook: when >25% spot eviction within 10m then:
  1) increase standby pool to 3 (per-az)
  2) set cluster-autoscaler gracefulDriftWindow=90s and scaleDownDelaySeconds=600 for standby pools
  3) run a quick taint-cleaner job to remove stale proxy=bootstrap taints older than 2m if they have no pods scheduled

kevin: can you add the taint-cleaner manifest? quick script idea:
```bash
# taint-cleaner: remove stale proxy=bootstrap if node is Ready and cordoned for >120s
kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.taints != null) | .metadata.name' | while read n; do
  age=$(kubectl get node $n -o jsonpath='{.metadata.creationTimestamp}')
  # pseudo: check taint timestamp and node readiness
  kubectl taint nodes $n node-role/proxy:NoSchedule- || true
done
```

ajay: i'll run a controlled chaos test in staging tomorrow 09:00 UTC to simulate batch spot waves. will report results in #eng-infra.

sophie: thanks — i'll own RFC + runbook and gate changes behind the staging chaos run.

kevin: :thumbsup: let's prioritize this for the asia spot instability run. small follow-ups: update cost dashboard and add a routed-fallback metric to alert on >5% request retries due to scheduling delays.
